hook_formulas: Named-concept title card: the caption is just the name of an idea ('The Von Restorff effect', 'Agrippas Trilemma', '#socrates'). Curiosity comes from the unfamiliar term.
Thinker + modern verdict: '[Philosopher] on [taboo topic]' with a blunt on-screen claim ('You can't win if you play fair' / Machiavelli on cheating).
Relatable one-liner punchline: 'Nothing is worse than thinking in 4k but speaking in 144p'.
Direct challenge or question to the viewer: 'Guess My Religion', 'Can you prove God exists without scripture?'.
Pop-culture lens: anime, Batman, Avatar, Kanye or athletes as the doorway to a life lesson.
Numbered trap/contrast: 'Two traps you need to avoid...', 'discipline vs devotion'.
Existential 'why' question titles on YouTube: 'Why Does Any of This Feel Normal', 'Is This All Life Is?'.
patterns.persona_voice: Earnest, introspective young man who has been alone a long time and read a lot. Speaks as 'an attempt rather than a verdict', but lands contrarian takes on effort, discipline, sex and religion. Leans on his own story: years of isolation, parents' basement, couch-surfing, 1,162 videos before 1,000 followers.
patterns.pacing_format: Short vertical talking-head clips, often green screen or text-on-screen over slowed+reverb or cinematic sounds. Many are filmed fast in one or two takes, including at night outdoors. Captions are frequently just the hook or hashtags. Very high volume: about 2,400 TikToks, and he describes 12 to 14 recordings a day early on.
recurring_themes: Gen Z men, romance and dating
philosophers made practical (Socrates, Nietzsche, Machiavelli, Dostoevsky)
religion, morality and later Christian faith
AI and beauty standards / modern life feeling abnormal
cta_patterns: Mostly no explicit CTA on TikTok; the question in the hook drives comments
YouTube clips point to the long original video
Bio routes to Instagram and email; Substack for long essays
Controversial takes invite stitches, which he acknowledges ('every time I get stitched a hundred times')
strategy_notes: Volume first: he posted 1,162 videos before reaching 1,000 followers, then grew fast.
Low-production batches can outperform polished ones: his eight one-take snow videos reportedly all reached hundreds of thousands of views.
Pivoted from feel-good comedy to philosophy and social commentary, but still mixes in light videos.
Uses podcasts (Modern Wisdom, Jack Neel, Barbarian Banter) to convert short-form reach into long-form authority.
Polarization is a growth engine: critic channels make whole videos about him, which keeps his name searched.
Trending/slowed sounds plus a single text line give emotional mood with almost no editing.
gaps: TikTok and Instagram pages could not be fetched directly, so most captions come from search snippets and several caption-to-ID matches are guesses.
No Instagram reel URLs were found.
View counts were rarely visible; most metrics are likes from snippets and unverified.
No app name was found despite a podcast mention.
Uploader of the 'Jett Franzen: ...' YouTube shorts is not confirmed.
